cards.intuition: Retries are inevitable, so make them harmless. The target after five executions over identical input should look exactly like the target after one.
cards.topic: Idempotent Writes: Same Input, Same Result

cards.intuition: Converge on one keyed state rather than accumulating attempts: overwrite an owned deterministic slice, merge by business key, stage and swap, or deduplicate by stable ID.
cards.formula: write effect must depend on data, not execution count
cards.topic: Idempotent Writes: Same Input, Same Result

cards.concept: Why idempotent writes alone are insufficient
cards.intuition: An overwrite still changes if transformation uses current time, unseeded randomness, mutable lookups, or fresh model output. The recipe and its ingredients must both be repeatable.
cards.formula: reproducible state = deterministic transform + idempotent sink
cards.topic: Idempotent Writes: Same Input, Same Result

cards.intuition: A worker may truncate only the complete slice it owns. Erasing a shared partition is repeatable but repeatedly destroys its neighbor's data.
cards.formula: overwrite scope must equal job ownership scope
cards.topic: Idempotent Writes: Same Input, Same Result

cards.intuition: The record itself carries the routing answer. Stable event date or a stable key hash sends it to the same destination regardless of retry time, machine, or arrival order.
Replaying Monday on Wednesday routes Monday's facts into Wednesday, leaving one partition wrong and polluting another. Event time keeps historical work aimed at history.
A stable hash reproduces placement but a whale key can still create a hot bucket. Repair skew through a better stable key or controlled rebucketing, not opportunistic placement.
cards.formula: stable assignment and uniform load are separate properties

cards.intuition: Full refresh rebuilds everything and heals old mistakes. Incremental refresh touches only changes and saves enormous work, but inherits bookkeeping and drift risks.
cards.formula: full = all history; incremental = new or changed slice

cards.intuition: A watermark is the bookmark recording the latest processed change position. The next run reads beyond it and applies the delta with an idempotent write.

cards.concept: Why use an incremental lookback window?
cards.intuition: Late visibility and clock skew can strand rows just behind the bookmark. Re-reading an overlapping tail catches them, and idempotency makes duplicate processing harmless.
cards.formula: read from watermark - lookback, then write idempotently

cards.concept: How do incremental pipelines observe deletes?
cards.intuition: A vanished row emits no updated_at delta, so its target copy becomes a ghost. Represent deletion as data through a soft-delete marker or consume a change log.
cards.formula: delete propagation requires tombstone, soft delete, or CDC

cards.intuition: Run cheap increments for daily operations, then periodically rebuild or reconcile against the source. The audit prevents small misses and ghosts from becoming permanent history.
